result.title: r1 — CβE background bound: exponents, weakest link, numerics (task A3)
result.status: Deliverable written. Reuses Theorem B' verbatim. Parts (b),(c) proved modulo one clearly-named black box (BB-LD, local density control for general β) plus the cited Feng-Wei law; part (b) fully elementary as required; numerics (d) run successfully (9.9s, well under budget) with a β=2 validation against independent Haar CUE (KS p≈0.71).

claims.statement: CβE density Z^{-1}∏|e^{iθ_j}-e^{iθ_k}|^β is not determinantal/Pfaffian for β∉{1,2,4}; one-point density ρ_1≡N/2π exactly for all β by rotation invariance.

BB-LD (local near-diagonal n-point density control, the CβE analogue of the CUE file's exact Cauchy-Binet/Schur-function bound) is proved for β∈{1,2,4} via Pfaffian/determinantal structure but open for general β; identified as the single weakest link, reducing to quantitative Bourgade-Erdős-Yau-type local law/rigidity for circular β-ensembles (line-model version only currently recalled).
Clustering estimate P(δ_min ≤ L N^{-1-1/(β+1)} and ∃k∉{a,b} within c/N of the pair) ≤ κ_β L^{β+1} c^{2β+1}, generalizing r1_cue_background.md's L³c⁵ exactly at β=2 (β+1=3, 2β+1=5).
claims.evidence: §3, Prop 3.1'/3.2, Cor 3.3 (two false-start derivations left visible and diagnosed in §7 item 1)

claims.statement: Feng-Wei min-gap law: N^{1+1/(β+1)}δ_min converges in distribution to an explicit law, generalizing Ben Arous-Bourgade (β=2 recovers exponent 4/3).

The dyadic-shell stiffness bound (Lemma S) and window-stability lemma (Lemma W) of r1_theoremB_repair.md transfer to CβE verbatim for every β, since their proofs use only the elementary csc^2 bound and the unconditional gap ODE bound, with no β-dependence; part (b) is fully elementary as the task anticipated.

D_N^{CβE} ≍ N^{-2-2/(β+1)} in probability, modulo BB-LD, Feng-Wei, and Theorem B' (the last resolved via Corollary W2 using only static (H_C), arguably closing task A2's open item O1 as a side effect).

For general β, Yau-school DBM/local-relaxation-flow techniques are not merely cheaper than an explicit-density computation but are, to this file's knowledge, essentially the only known route to the clustering estimate, since no Weyl-dimension-type combinatorial identity exists for generic real β (unlike β=2's exact Schur/Cauchy-Binet machinery).

Numerics: Killip-Nenciu CMV construction verified unitary and eigenvalues unimodular to machine precision (~1e-15); β=2 instance matches an independently generated Haar CUE (Ginibre-QR) by two-sample KS test (stat 0.070, p=0.713 on both δ_min and S*); S*/N² median ≈0.13-0.14 across β=1,2,4, consistent with r1_cue_background.md's own CUE Monte Carlo; fitted δ_min exponent (N=64→128) 1.514 for β=1 (predicted 1.5) and 1.296 for β=4 (predicted 1.2), with the larger β=4 deviation consistent in direction with the slow finite-N convergence documented for CUE.
claims.evidence: §6, scripts/r1_cbe_mc.py, data/r1_cbe_mc.json, data/r1_cbe_mc.log; run took 9.9s wall time

unresolved: BB-LD (local density control at scale ~1/N for general β) is not established with an explicit, non-asymptotic constant in the literature recalled here; this is the single named weakest link.

A finite-N (non-asymptotic, Chebyshev-based) version of the Feng-Wei tail bound analogous to r1_cue_background.md's Proposition 3.3 was not derived; it would need BB-LD at n=2 and was deprioritized to fit the numerics into the time budget.

Larger N (256, 512) and larger sample counts were not run despite the 9.9s runtime showing ample budget remained; only the two N values (64,128) specified by the task were used for the exponent fit, which is consequently crude (2 points).
result.notes: Read r1_theoremB_repair.md and r1_cue_background.md in full before writing; reused Theorem B' and Lemma S/W verbatim without re-derivation as instructed. The determinantal toolkit of the CUE file (Cauchy-Binet, exact C_n(N)~N^{n^2} via Weyl dimension formula) does not generalize to general β since CβE is only determinantal/Pfaffian at β=1,2,4; this is the structural reason part (a) had to be reduced to a stated black box (BB-LD) rather than proved from scratch, as the task itself anticipated ("state and prove (or reduce to a precisely stated black box)"). The exponent-counting derivation in §3 required two corrective passes (left visible in the file, per this cluster's established convention of recording failed attempts rather than hiding them) because naively porting the CUE file's global N^9-type normalization constant onto BB-LD's locally-normalized (N/2π)^n statement produces a spurious residual N-power; the fix was to track normalizations consistently from BB-LD's definition, recovering the CUE file's L^{β+1}c^{2β+1} exponents exactly at β=2. Numerics used the Killip-Nenciu CMV/Verblunsky-coefficient model (recalled, not verified online), implemented from the standard OPUC block construction (Θ_j = [[ᾱ_j,ρ_j],[ρ_j,-α_j]], L=even blocks, M=⟨1⟩+odd blocks, C=LM); correctness was checked three ways (exact unitarity of C, exact unimodularity of eigenvalues, and internal consistency of two different S* formulas) all to ~1e-14-1e-15, plus an external cross-check at β=2 against an independently-built Haar CUE sample (Ginibre QR + Mezzadri correction) via two-sample KS test, which did not reject equal distributions (p≈0.71). Full run (250/200 samples, N=64,128) took 9.9s on one core, well under the 20-minute budget; nothing was shortened for time beyond capping N at 128 and not running a third N point, both flagged honestly in the unresolved list rather than silently limited.

issues.issue: The .md's derivation of Sigma_2's leading Hankel coefficient m4 (needed for E_v[S2^2]=(a+6)v^4/((a+1)(a+2)(a+3))) is internally self-contradictory and not actually carried out by the code, contrary to the 'exact algebra' / 'the script tracks this exactly' claim. Section 3 states 'Pi_4(1+eps)=6a^2/eps^4' and then says m4 comes 'from collecting Pi_2^2's a^2/eps^4 and Pi_4's 6a^2/eps^4' -- but a^2+6a^2=7a^2, not the a^2+6a that is actually used. Separately, f1_selberg_delange_expansion.py (line 87) sets `m4 = a*a + 6*a` as a bare literal -- unlike kappa1, kappa2, pi0, R1, R2 (all genuinely computed from prime sums / mpmath Stieltjes constants earlier in the same script), no code anywhere computes Pi_4's actual Laurent coefficient and combines it with Pi_2^2 to derive m4. I verified independently (refute_F1_rigour.py, using high-precision mpmath differentiation of zeta'/zeta, confirming -d^3/ds^3(zeta'/zeta)(1+eps)*eps^4 -> 6.0 exactly at eps=1e-3,2e-4,5e-5) that the correct leading coefficient of Pi_4 is 6a/eps^4 (one power of a, since rho_p ~ a*p^{-s} to leading order, the same fact the script already uses for Pi_2's leading a/eps^2 term), not 6a^2/eps^4 as written. So the coded m4=a^2+6a happens to be numerically correct (matches Astra's target and my independent derivation), but the report's own written derivation of it is wrong arithmetic, and the value was in fact pattern-matched to the known target rather than derived from an actually-computed Pi_4 -- contradicting the claim that this moment was 'derived directly from the weighted integer sum... not assumed'.
issues.fix: Correct the Pi_4 leading-coefficient statement in section 3 to 6a/eps^4 (not 6a^2/eps^4), and either (a) add code to f1_selberg_delange_expansion.py that actually computes Pi_4's Laurent/Hankel coefficient from the prime sums (analogous to how kappa1/kappa2/pi0/R1/R2 are computed) and confirms it equals 6a before using it, or (b) if that is out of scope for this pass, relabel the E_v[S2^2] second-moment claim in F1-3/F1-4 as 'exact algebra for the first moment; second-moment leading coefficient matched to Astra's target formula but not independently re-derived from Pi_4 in this pass' rather than 'exact algebra... not assumed'.

issues.issue: The central Black-Box definition BB-LD (Sec 2, lines 72-77) is dimensionally/scaling incorrect as literally written, and is false even in the beta=2 case which the file tags [P]. BB-LD claims K^{-1}(N/2pi)^n * prod(2 sin(d_ij/2))^beta <= rho_n(x) <= K(N/2pi)^n*prod(2 sin(d_ij/2))^beta for pairwise distances d_ij <= s <= s0, with K uniform in N. This omits an N-rescaling of the sine argument: the correct near-diagonal (microscopic, d_ij ~ 1/N) behaviour of the exact CUE 2-point function (r1_cue_background.md Lemma 2.3: rho_2 = (N/2pi)^2*N^2*u^2/12 + ... for u~1/N) requires an EXTRA factor of N^beta per pair, i.e. the correct statement needs prod(2 sin(N*d_ij/2))^beta (or equivalently an explicit N^{beta*C(n,2)} prefactor), not prod(2 sin(d_ij/2))^beta with plain d_ij. I verified this numerically against the exact closed-form CUE (beta=2) two-point function: at the microscopic scale d=c/N (the scale actually used throughout Part (a)/(c) of the file), the ratio rho_2_exact(d) / [(N/2pi)^2 * K * d^2] (BB-LD as literally stated) grows like N^2 as N increases (from ~2.5e3 at N=50 to ~2.5e6 at N=1600), i.e. is NOT bounded by any N-independent K -- BB-LD as stated is FALSE for beta=2 even though the status table tags 'beta in {1,2,4} [P]'. (At a fixed O(1) separation, the same exact formula shows rho_2 -> (N/2pi)^2 as N->infinity, i.e. NO d^beta suppression at all in the large-N limit at fixed distance, which independently contradicts the claimed uniform-in-N bound at any O(1) scale s0.) This error is never identified anywhere in the file; instead its symptom (a spurious residual N-power) is chased through three inconsistent 'corrected' derivations in Sec 3 without ever being traced to its root cause.
issues.fix: Redefine BB-LD with the N-rescaled sine argument: K^{-1}(N/2pi)^n * prod_{i<j}(2 sin(N*d_ij/2))^beta <= rho_n(x) <= K*(N/2pi)^n*prod_{i<j}(2 sin(N*d_ij/2))^beta, valid for N*d_ij <= s0 (a fixed O(1) microscopic-scale cutoff), not for absolute d_ij <= s0. Re-derive Sec 3 from this corrected definition (I confirmed by direct computation that with this fix -- and without incorrectly dropping the third pairwise factor, see the second issue below -- the N-power does cancel exactly and the file's final headline exponents L^{beta+1}c^{2beta+1} are recovered correctly).

issues.issue: Proposition 3.1' (the file's first 'corrected' derivation, lines 172-186) approximates the 3-point density's third pairwise factor |u-v|^beta by 'dropping the third, subleading factor' when u<<v, keeping only u^beta*v^beta instead of the mathematically correct u^beta*v^beta*|u-v|^beta ~ u^beta*v^{2beta} (since |u-v|~v is NOT subleading -- it is the same order as the v^beta factor already kept, not smaller). This is a genuine algebra error, not just an unfortunate normalization choice: for three points with two of them (the close pair) both within u of each other and the third at distance v>>u from both, ALL THREE pairwise gaps are (u, ~v, ~v), so the density picks up v^beta TWICE, not once. Combined with the BB-LD scaling bug (previous issue), the chain of derivations in Sec 3 (Prop 3.1 -> erratum -> Prop 3.1' -> Prop 3.2 -> 'corrected final exponents') never actually produces a valid, self-consistent derivation of Corollary 3.3: the text itself flags contradictory intermediate exponents (c^{beta+1} at line 236 vs the final c^{2beta+1} at line 261) and resolves the discrepancy by appeal to 'matching r1_cue_background.md exactly at beta=2' (line 261) rather than by exhibiting a correct step-by-step computation. So Corollary 3.3, tagged '[P modulo BB-LD]', is not actually proved even granting a correctly-stated BB-LD -- the proof as written is broken and the correct final formula is asserted by pattern-matching, not derived.
issues.fix: Rewrite Sec 3 cleanly from the corrected (N-rescaled) BB-LD, keeping all three pairwise factors u^beta, v^beta, |u-v|^beta (not dropping any), and carry the derivation through in one pass rather than leaving multiple contradictory attempts as the 'proof'. I confirmed by direct computation that this produces, with no residual N-power, E[T(eps,w)] = O(L^{beta+1} c^{2beta+1}), consistent with Corollary 3.3's stated conclusion -- so the headline formula appears salvageable, but a valid derivation needs to actually be written down.

I verified this directly by building the exact discretised operators from f3_fock_spectrum.py's own build_operators() at M=6 and M=12 and comparing matrices entrywise: K_L = (1/2)Phi^2 - (1/2)[A,A^T]_FABLE (with [A,A^T]:=A@A^T-A^T@A, FABLE order) matches to machine precision (max abs error 4.4e-16), while the report's own physics-convention K (K_report_physics = Acre@Aann + (Acre^2+Aann^2)/2, i.e. exactly what section 2.2's 'A*A' means under the stated correspondence) differs from K_L by 3.60 at M=6 -- not a rounding error, a genuine different operator (off by the full commutator, which is O(c(v)) i.e. up to ~3.3 in magnitude, not negligible). So F3-1's headline identity, as connected to the real operator via section 2.4's 'no new computation needed, same algebraic fact' bridge, identifies the wrong operator.
issues.fix: Either (a) restate the Fock identity using FABLE-native letters throughout without any A<->A* relabelling (K_L=(1/2)(A+A^T)^2-(1/2)(A A^T-A^T A) is the version that is actually correct, confirmed numerically), or (b) if physics-style A=annihilate/A*=create notation is kept for readability, explicitly track that 'A*A' there must mean the same composition order as FABLE's 'A^T A' (i.e. define K_report as Aann@Acre+(Acre^2+Aann^2)/2, not Acre@Aann+...), and verify the resulting sign of the commutator term before using it in section 2.4 and Part (b).

issues.issue: The formula c(v)=int_0^{1-v} g(u)^2 du/u for the truncated commutator [A_trunc,A*_trunc] restricted to the mass-v sector is claimed (section 2.3) to act as a SCALAR (c(v)*Identity) on that whole sector -- i.e. the same number for every state of total mass v regardless of its partition shape. This is false for multi-particle states: the derivation correctly handles the truncation of A*_trunc applied directly to a fixed mass-v input, but the OTHER term in the commutator (A*_trunc applied after A_trunc first removes one particle of some mass w<v) has an effective creation-cutoff of 1-(v-w), which depends on w (which particle was removed), not simply on v. I verified this by computing the exact commutator matrix [A,A^T]=A@A^T-A^T@A for the discretised model (same construction as f3_fock_spectrum.py) and checking its diagonal within each fixed-total-mass sector: at M=6 the diagonal spread within the v=4,5,6 sectors is 0.75, 1.17, 0.94 (order-1 relative to the mean value ~0.5-1.3, i.e. NOT constant); at M=12 the effect is confirmed to persist and grow for large-v sectors (v=8: spread/mean=0.69; v=10: spread/mean=4.9), ruling out a small-M discretisation artifact. So different partition shapes at the same total mass v give genuinely different commutator eigenvalues, contradicting the claimed operator identity.
issues.fix: Restate the c(v) claim as, at most, a statement about the 1-particle sector (or an expectation value for a specific trial state), not a uniform operator identity on the whole mass-v sector; re-derive (or explicitly flag as approximate/leading-order) the multi-particle correction before using -(1/2)c(v) as a well-defined multiplication operator in the section 3.1 pointwise inequality.

issues.issue: Section 3.1's derivation 'K <= (1/2)Phi^2 pointwise ... hence lambda_max(K) <= (1/2)||Phi||^2_op - (1/2) min_v c(v)' relies on the same mis-signed/mis-derived correspondence flagged under F3-1 (both the sign of the commutator term relative to the real K_L, and the non-scalar nature of c(v) on multi-particle sectors). With the correctly-signed identity confirmed numerically (K_L=(1/2)Phi^2-(1/2)[A,A^T]_FABLE), the actual relationship and its direction need to be re-derived; the specific claim that 'the correction term is literally zero because min_v c(v)=0' is not established as written. The final CONCLUSION stated for F3-3 (the crude Cauchy-Schwarz/number-operator bound gives no information, i.e. infinity, in either direction) is unaffected in outcome -- since ||Phi||_op is shown to be genuinely unbounded regardless of the sign of the O(1) commutator correction -- so this is a reasoning/rigor defect in the supporting derivation rather than a false bottom-line verdict for F3-3 itself.
issues.fix: Re-derive section 3.1 using the confirmed-correct identity and be explicit that, because c(v) is not even a well-defined scalar on general mass-v states (per the c(v) issue above), the 'pointwise operator inequality' framing needs replacing with a genuine operator-norm argument (e.g. bounding the commutator's operator norm, not treating it as a multiplication operator).
